clues: Possesses an antiphagocytic Vi capsular polysaccharide antigen and resides exclusively in human hosts.
Invades ileal Peyer patches via M cells and survives inside reticuloendothelial macrophages.
The motile, H2S-producing Gram-negative bacillus responsible for classical typhoid fever.
Overlain by specialized antigen-sampling microfold (M) cells in the lamina propria.
Become hyperplastic during the first two weeks of enteric fever and undergo necrosis in week three.
Aggregated lymphoid nodules concentrated in the terminal ileum where longitudinal typhoid ulcers and perforations occur.
Measures serum agglutinating antibodies against somatic O and flagellar H antigens.
Frequently yields false positives in endemic regions due to baseline immunity, vaccination, or malaria.
A serological agglutination assay historically used to support the diagnosis of enteric fever.
Non-motile, non-lactose-fermenting, H2S-negative members of the family Enterobacteriaceae.
Requires an ultra-low infectious dose of 10 to 100 organisms and spreads cell-to-cell via host actin tails.
The invasive bacterial genus responsible for acute bacillary dysentery with mucoid bloody stools.
Adheres to small bowel enterocytes via colonization factor antigens without causing mucosal ulceration.
Secretes plasmid-encoded heat-labile (LT) and heat-stable (ST) enterotoxins.
The leading bacterial cause of travellers' diarrhoea and infantile watery diarrhoea in developing regions.

terms.sub: Cholera and Other Foodborne Bacterial Gastroenteritis
clues: Grows as flat yellow sucrose-fermenting colonies on alkaline TCBS agar.
Appears as a comma-shaped, oxidase-positive Gram-negative rod with a single polar flagellum.
The waterborne pathogen whose enterotoxin elevates cAMP to produce profuse rice-water secretory diarrhoea.
Possesses a segmented 11-segment double-stranded RNA genome and a wheel-like capsid.
Secretes the NSP4 viral enterotoxin and blunts small intestinal villi.
The leading global viral cause of severe dehydrating watery diarrhoea in infants and young children.

terms.sub: Intestinal Protozoa: Amoebiasis, Giardiasis, and Cryptosporidiosis
clues: Diagnostic motile trophozoites in dysenteric stool contain phagocytosed red blood cells.
Produces flask-shaped ulcers in the colon and anchovy-paste liver abscesses.
The tissue-invasive anaerobic protozoan transmitted via quadrinucleate cysts that causes amoebic dysentery.

terms.sub: Intestinal Protozoa: Amoebiasis, Giardiasis, and Cryptosporidiosis
clues: Trophozoites possess two nuclei, four pairs of flagella, and a ventral adhesive sucking disc.
Causes non-invasive duodenal brush-border malabsorption without blood or pus in the stool.
A flagellated intestinal protozoan that causes foul-smelling, greasy steatorrhoea and bloating.

terms.sub: Intestinal Helminths: Nematodes, Cestodes, and Trematodes
clues: Larvae migrate through the liver and lungs, triggering Loeffler eosinophilic pneumonitis.
Diagnosed by identifying mammillated, bile-stained fertilized eggs on stool microscopy.
The largest human intestinal roundworm, capable of causing mechanical small bowel or biliary obstruction.
